clue.text: Peak hire charge for current tumbling down

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor
rent is the charge paid to hire a property

explanation.surface: A mountain-hut owner bumps up the fees just as the meltwater comes crashing down.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a word used in south-west England for a craggy hilltop; 'for' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushing, violent stream of water is exactly what a fast flow tumbling downhill is called.

clue.text: Marks made on leaving

parts.note: footprints are marks made as one walks away, and to make these is also to depart

explanation.surface: Someone notices the marks a departing visitor has left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'make tracks' is to leave, and the prints left behind are also the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Footprints or trails left by someone departing are what 'making tracks' produces.

clue.text: About the Thespian of Windscale

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a Thespian, after Thespis, is an actor

explanation.surface: A piece about a famous actor from the Cumbrian town of Windscale.
explanation.walkthrough: Windscale (now Sellafield) in Cumbria is the British nuclear site where a reactor caught fire in 1957; the definition is 'the [thing] of Windscale'.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscale was Britain's early nuclear plant, famous for the 1957 fire in its atomic pile.

clue.text: Iris-tints worn by some poker-players?

explanation.surface: A question about the colouring of the eyes of card-players at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Shades of the iris are tints of the eyes, and the green visors worn by card dealers and players also go by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tints of the iris are shades of the eye, and visors shielding a card-player's brow are known by the same name.

clue.text: Figuratively describing the partiality of the entire jury

definitions.text: Figuratively describing the partiality of the entire jury

parts.words: Figuratively describing the partiality of the entire jury
parts.note: a jury has twelve members, and partiality is taking sides, so a whole jury that is partial would have twelve of them

explanation.surface: A lawyer complains that the whole jury is biased.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the answer is a geometric word for a dodecagon; here a jury of twelve, each taking a side, is pictured that way.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape with a dozen faces bears this name, and a jury of twelve each taking a side fits it figuratively.

clue.text: Robes altered for King Edward to be less tight

indicators.note: altered says the letters of robes are changed into a new order

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher of a King Edward

explanation.surface: A tailor lets out the royal robes so that the king can breathe more easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges ROBES to SOBER; 'tight' here means drunk, not snug, so 'less tight' is more sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, so someone less tight is in a more sober state.

clue.text: Evil Nile god's clique

explanation.surface: A question about the circle of followers around an evil Egyptian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Set (or Seth) is the Egyptian god of chaos who murdered Osiris; the word is also a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian god of chaos and the desert bears this name, and it also means a group or circle of people.

clue.text: Music-maker to interdict Miss March

parts.note: to interdict is to forbid, ban
Jo March is the heroine of Little Women

explanation.surface: A musician is forbidden to play by a woman named March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; Miss March is Jo, one of the four March sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: This strummed, round-bodied stringed instrument is a maker of music.

clue.text: Composer got Lawrence's alias in one

parts.note: T.E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer took on the false name that Lawrence of Arabia used.
explanation.walkthrough: After the war T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) enlisted as Aircraftman Ross; 'got' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini, who wrote The Barber of Seville and William Tell, was an Italian opera composer.

clue.text: Continuing noisy rant about eastern issue

indicators.note: about means the word rant goes round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: a son is a man's issue, his offspring

explanation.surface: A loud, unbroken tirade about some problem in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the noisy outburst wraps round the abbreviation and the offspring. 'Continuing noisy' describes a sound that rings on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that rings and lingers loudly, echoing on, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: A labyrinth intended, say, to cause wonder

parts.note: a labyrinth is a maze

indicators.note: say marks that the word for intended is to be heard, giving only its sound

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A garden maze has been built deliberately to astonish its visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you MEANT is only heard, so it is written MENT; 'to cause' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonder in the sense of astonished surprise is a synonym for the feeling the answer names.

clue.text: Found in a Limerick man's beard

definitions.text: Found in a Limerick man's beard

parts.words: Found in a Limerick man's beard
parts.note: Edward Lear's limerick about an old man with a beard ends with owls, a hen, larks and a wren building their homes in it

explanation.surface: A curious discovery in the whiskers of an Irishman from Limerick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limerick' looks like the Irish city; it is the comic verse form, and Edward Lear's best-known limerick has birds building in an old man's beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build homes of twigs and moss, and in Lear's verse four kinds of bird set them up in the beard.

clue.text: Jack was skilled in' execution of craft

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack was an expert at handling his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was the notorious executioner of Charles II's reign, whose name became a byword for hangmen; 'of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The infamous hangman Jack bore this surname, and it is also a two-masted sailing boat, a craft.

clue.text: Like the state 'ot Australia in the last century ?

explanation.surface: A question about how an Australian state looked a hundred years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in the 1900s, 'the last century' is the 19th, the reign of Queen Victoria; Victoria is also a state of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from Victoria, the south-eastern Australian state, and something of Queen Victoria's 19th-century era share this adjective.

clue.text: News of explosion of gang warfare ?

definitions.text: News of explosion of gang warfare

parts.words: News of explosion of gang warfare
parts.note: a report is both a news account and the bang of a gun, so a news item on gangsters could be this

explanation.surface: Headlines tell of an outbreak of violence between rival gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: A report is also the bang of a gun going off, so 'explosion' plays on that second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item about a gang shoot-out is a piece of journalism on lawbreaking, and a gun's bang is also called a report.

clue.text: Into net ? Despair ! Anyhow che sarà sarà

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old order, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A footballer watches the ball go into his own net and shrugs: whatever will be, will be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' rearranges the fourteen letters of INTO NET and DESPAIR. 'Che sarà sarà' is Italian for 'what will be, will be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fatalist motto 'what will be, will be' expresses the doctrine that every event is fixed in advance.

clue.text: Removes Jack's pamphlets

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, an AB (able seaman), so Jack's gives ABS
tracts are pamphlets, especially religious ones

explanation.surface: A sailor's leaflets are taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a sailor, and sailors are ABs (able-bodied seamen); 'Jack's' gives AB'S.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to take it away or extract it.

clue.text: The faculty of judgment is so decisive

definitions.text: The faculty of judgment is so

explanation.surface: The power of judgment is claimed to be the deciding factor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'critical faculty' is the power of judgment, and a critical moment is a decisive one.
explanation.definitionFit: Judging merit is the work of the critical faculty, and a turning point that decides the outcome is a critical one.

clue.text: New rendering is not authorized

parts.note: the 1880s English Bible translation made to update the 1611 King James Bible, which is known as the Authorized Version

explanation.surface: A new performance of a song has gone ahead without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authorized' points at the Authorized (King James) Version of the Bible; the later translation that replaced it is literally a new version, not the Authorized one.
explanation.definitionFit: A translation that updated the 1611 Bible is a new rendering, distinct from the Authorized Version.

clue.text: Books of visual speech ?

explanation.surface: A question about books that speak to the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Volumes are books, and a look that 'speaks volumes' says a great deal without words: speech one sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomes are another word for books, and a telling look is said to speak a great quantity without sound.

clue.text: Like a company producing cattle-food

parts.note: a firm that pressed seed for its fuel and also sold the pressed residue for feed would be both kinds of business

explanation.surface: A firm that makes feed for cows.
explanation.walkthrough: The cattle feed is pressed seed residue left after extracting the fat; a company could be an 'oil' company like a 'cake' company.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed linseed or cottonseed left after extracting its fat is a fodder cake fed to cattle.

clue.text: Red and black seaport

parts.note: a Soviet, hence communist red, port on the Black Sea

explanation.surface: A harbour town painted in red and black colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red and black' suggests colours; 'Red' means Soviet communist, and 'black' points to the Black Sea, on which this Ukrainian port lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Black Sea port, then in the Soviet Union, is now in Ukraine.

clue.text: Where martyrs combined against the law

definitions.text: Where martyrs combined against the law

parts.words: Where martyrs combined against the law
parts.note: the Dorset village whose farm labourers were transported in 1834 for forming a trade union

explanation.surface: A question about the place where persecuted believers banded together in defiance of the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combined' means formed a combination, a trade union, which was effectively illegal in 1834; the Dorset labourers transported for it are known as the martyrs of this village.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset village gave its name to the six martyrs of 1834, early heroes of British trade unionism.

clue.text: London rail terminus set vertically

explanation.surface: A London railway station placed upright.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways the 'up' line runs towards London, so the London terminus is the up end; to upend is to stand on end.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a line toward London is the 'up' end, and to stand something on its end is to tip it upright.

clue.text: Drew the line as umpire?

parts.note: an umpire gives decisions, and a ruler is used to draw straight lines, so both senses describe one verb

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire finally refuses to tolerate any more bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew the line' looks like setting a limit; it is literally drawing a straight line, and an umpire who decides has given a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both marking straight lines on paper and giving an official decision, as an umpire does.

clue.text: Search east of the valley

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A search party sets off east of the valley to look for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' links; a combe is a short steep valley, a word common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a West Country word for a short, steep-sided hollow or dale in a hillside.

clue.text: Men of war mainly wore armour

definitions.text: Men of war mainly wore armour

parts.words: Men of war mainly wore armour
parts.note: men-of-war are warships, and 'mainly' means on the main, the open sea, where these ships were plated with metal

explanation.surface: Soldiers going into battle were mostly clad in armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men of war' suggests soldiers, but a man-of-war is a warship; 'mainly' is 'on the main' (the sea), and nineteenth-century warships wore metal plating.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam warships plated with metal armour were named for their protective cladding.

clue.text: Climbing, one of her extra-mural activities ?

definitions.text: Climbing, one of her extra-mural activities

parts.words: Climbing, one of her extra-mural activities
parts.note: a creeper climbs the outside of walls, which is extra-mural in the literal sense, and plants of this kind were often called 'she'

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's hobbies outside school include rock climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra-mural' means outside the walls; the evergreen creeper climbs the outsides of walls, and the clue gives the plant a female name as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen creeper climbs over walls, and it is also a girl's name, so 'her' fits.

clue.text: Date when judgment has been promised

definitions.text: Date when judgment has been promised

parts.words: Date when judgment has been promised
parts.note: the end of the world, when Christian teaching says all will be judged

explanation.surface: A court has promised a date on which it will deliver its verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judgment' sounds like a court case, but it is the Last Judgment, and the final day of the world when it is promised to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomsday, the end of the world on which the Last Judgment is foretold, goes by this name.

clue.text: War-god put back in mosaic

indicators.note: back says the words for the god and for put together are read from right to left

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
set means put, placed

explanation.surface: A figure of the god of war has been put back into place in a mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ARES and SET together, giving TES SERA; 'in' links, and the answer is a tile that makes up a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles of stone or glass from which a mosaic is assembled.
